# Postgres without a server

[PGlite](https://pglite.dev/) is Postgres 17 compiled to WebAssembly, which runs the whole database
engine inside a JavaScript process, with no server, port or Docker container. Tests that would
otherwise need a running Postgres can start one in-process instead.
[py-pglite](https://pypi.org/project/py-pglite/) starts PGlite from Python in about two seconds and
puts a socket in front of it that speaks the Postgres wire protocol, so psycopg and SQLAlchemy can
connect to it.

## Compatibility

PGlite bundles pgvector, so the lab's experiments run unchanged. `Base.metadata.create_all` creates
the `documents` table with its `Vector(1536)` column and the JSONB `events` table, and distances,
nearest-neighbor queries and an HNSW index all work inside WebAssembly.

## Limitations

- PGlite serves one connection at a time. While the notebook was being written, a second
  simultaneous connection crashed psycopg, so all queries go through one shared engine.
- In py-pglite 0.5.3, a message above about 6 KB breaks the bridge. A 1536-dimension vector is
  larger than that, so it has to be generated on the server side, or replaced by a smaller one.
- PGlite runs at roughly half native speed, which is fine for tests and too slow for benchmarks.
- Starting or stopping a manager kills every PGlite process on the machine, including one that a
  notebook or another test run is using.

## Test databases

A test suite can share one PGlite database for the whole session. `create_all` runs once, and each
test runs inside a transaction that is rolled back at the end, so every test starts from the same
state:

```python
@pytest.fixture
def session(engine):
    with engine.connect() as conn:
        trans = conn.begin()
        yield Session(bind=conn)
        trans.rollback()
```

PGlite covers the SQL that tests usually exercise, while anything that depends on several
connections or on real timings still needs a Postgres container:

| need | PGlite | Docker Postgres |
|---|---|---|
| unit tests and CI without services | yes, about 2 s to start | slower, needs Docker |
| SQL, JSONB and pgvector parity | yes, the same Postgres core | yes |
| concurrency, locks, PgBouncer, replication, timings | no | yes |
| large payloads from Python | not through py-pglite 0.5.3 | yes |
